note: Vocabulary, exemptions, and per-language normalization data for prose_lint.py, which documents each section and the repository-local .prose-gate.json that may add exemptions.

charset.summary: a non-ASCII character its tier does not permit here

charset-unknown.summary: non-ASCII in no tier, bar a Latin letter and its U+0300-U+036F diacritics

semicolon.summary: a semicolon in prose, outside a series or labeled pair carrying a comma

dash.summary: a spaced hyphen joining or interrupting a sentence

comment-wrap.summary: a comment sentence wrapped across lines, or two on one line

comment-case.summary: a comment sentence opening in lowercase

comment-added.summary: a comment line this change adds or edits, opening its own line

sentence-length.summary: a sentence over the word cap

spelling.summary: a British spelling where the repo convention is US English

home-path.summary: an absolute home path naming a real account

dead-path.summary: a mention of a path git once tracked and the tree no longer holds

issue-ref.summary: an issue or pull request reference in a leading comment, a Python docstring, or instruction text

messages.charset-unknown: {name} (U+{code}) is in no tier - classify it in ptr727/ProjectTemplate: the comment-and-doc-style skill's "Character set" section and prose-gate.json's charset tiers
messages.semicolon: semicolon in prose -> a comma or two sentences
messages.dash: spaced hyphen -> a comma, two sentences, or parentheses
messages.comment-run-on: two sentences on one comment line -> split them
messages.comment-wrap: comment sentence wraps into the next line -> one sentence per line
messages.comment-case: comment sentence opens in lowercase -> capitalize, or restructure so it does not open on a lowercase name
messages.comment-added: a comment line this change adds or edits -> delete it, or allow it: the {label!r} label on the pull request, {env} at a commit, --allow-comments on a run by hand
messages.sentence-split: sentence wraps across lines (one sentence per line)
messages.sentence-length: {words} words in one sentence -> sentences of {cap} words or fewer
messages.home-path: absolute home path {path!r} -> use a constructed path, not an observed one
messages.dead-path: path {token!r} is deleted from this tree -> re-point, rewrite, or remove the stale mention
messages.issue-ref: issue or pull request reference {ref!r} -> state the constraint it stands for, or drop the clause
messages.error-empty-exclude: --exclude was given an empty value, which matches every path and would report a whole-tree scan as clean. Drop the blank entry rather than passing it, the way the composite action skips a blank line in .github/prose-gate-excludes.
messages.error-not-a-path: requested path(s) are not a file or a directory: {paths}. Refusing rather than falling back to the current directory, which would scan one tree and choose the rule set from another.
messages.error-many-repositories: the requested paths span more than one repository ({roots}). Each declares its own workflow model, so no single rule set is correct for all of them. Run the gate once per repository.
messages.error-no-diff: cannot diff against {base!r}, so the run cannot be scoped to changed lines. Refusing to scan the whole tree instead, since that reports the existing backlog as though this change introduced it. Check the ref exists and that the checkout carries its history.
messages.error-unread-diff: the diff against {base!r} names {count} readable file(s) this run was asked about, and the scan matched none of them: {paths}. Refusing to report a clean run, since a gate that read nothing is indistinguishable from a gate with nothing to read. Check that the run starts at the repository top level and that the requested paths cover the change.
messages.note-allowed: comment-added stood down by {named}. In CI the composite action passes that flag from its own input instead, which the fleet's caller computes from the {label!r} label and from the run being a release-model promotion, and it clears {env} so a runner cannot decide one.
messages.note-no-diff: comment-added is not checked without --diff, which is what tells an added comment apart from one the tree already held. Scope the run to a base to run it.
messages.note-shallow: dead-path is not checked in a shallow clone, which holds no deletion history to key on. Fetch the full history to run it.
messages.scope-whole: scope: {read} file(s) read, whole tree, gate {gate}
messages.scope-diff: scope: {read} of {discovered} file(s) read, {lines} changed line(s), diff against {base!r}, gate {gate}
messages.scope-plain: , {count} file(s) with no lexer read as plain text: {paths}
messages.scope-undecoded: , {count} file(s) the gate could not open or decode as UTF-8, so no rule read them: {paths}

--list-files.help: print the discovered file set and exit, for auditing the sweep scope

--diff.help: only report violations on lines changed vs BASE (matches the repo policy: fix as each file is next edited, not swept)

--allow-comments.help: stand `comment-added` down, for a change whose comment lines are wanted. PROSE_ALLOW_COMMENTS set to anything but a false spelling does the same, for a caller with nowhere to pass a flag. What makes a CI run pass it is the calling workflow's own condition

--provenance.help: name this copy of the gate on the verdict, as the composite action's owner/repo@ref, so a finding can be attributed to the commit that raised it
